pairs.difference: A: low camera, the ball sits in rippled sand with a dune line behind it, so ground and backdrop separate as in the real cards. B: high camera looking down, the cap almost faces the lens, sand fills the whole card with no horizon, and the ball's lower half swells toward the viewer.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to just above the ball's middle. Show a clear line where the sand ends and the backdrop starts in the upper third, with the cap tilted away near the top of the ball.

pairs.difference: A: straight-on, one view. The frame's inner posts recede evenly to one centre and the target turns only slightly on the shelf. B: the target is a thick disc swung hard to the left with a heavy blue side, while the bear and the frame face straight forward, so the parts do not share one view. Cans, ball and flag crowd in as extra depth steps.
pairs.fix: Turn the target only slightly so its side edge is a thin rim. Keep frame, target and bear in the same straight-on view on a plain shelf, with no extra props.

pairs.difference: A: wide-angle look from below. The unit's top edge falls steeply left, the right end swells toward the viewer, and the ceiling cornice races away. Window, plant, books and sofa add cropped foreground layers. B: mild perspective, one wall, one ceiling line, hero alone on a simpler background.
pairs.fix: Use a mild view with gentle slope on the unit's top edge. Show one plain striped wall behind it, and remove the sofa, plant and window.

pairs.difference: A: the sand reads as one plane at one angle, with the chest, shell and coins all sitting on it. B: the sand is a slope rising to the left and stops abruptly at the left card edge against the water, and the chest's right corner hangs over the falling ground, so the hero does not stand squarely on it.
pairs.fix: Lay the sand as one level seabed across the full card width, with the back edge horizontal, and rest all four chest corners flat on it.

pairs.difference: A: floorboards recede gently behind a low plank wall, so the space is shallow and the hat fills the card. B: a room corner with two walls meeting and floorboards running on steep diagonals. That gives strong convergence and a deep space with the hat small inside it, and the two wall planes turn away sharply.
pairs.fix: Remove the room corner. Put one flat plank wall straight behind the hat, with floorboards at a gentle angle, and bring the hat larger in the card.

pairs.difference: A: raised camera, with the booth widening toward the top, a swollen dome and a thick base slab seen from above, plus a broad floor area. B: lower camera with near-parallel verticals, flat even side faces and a shallow floor band, closer to the real mild perspective.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to mid-booth height and keep the booth's corner lines nearly parallel. Flatten the roof dome and show only a thin strip of the base top.

pairs.difference: A: consistent raised view, with floorboards converging toward one horizon and gloves laid along it with cast shadows. B: floor-level close-up, the front glove swells into a huge rounded mass cut off from the back one, the table plane is almost edge-on, and the background wall goes soft and photographic.
pairs.fix: Raise the camera so the floor is clearly visible as a surface, with boards running back. Keep both gloves at similar size, with the background flat and crisp rather than out of focus.

pairs.difference: Both show the pair of fins from the same raised three-quarter angle on a flat ring background with no ground. Foreshortening toward the heels is similar and each pair shares one view. Only size in the card differs, which is not a camera issue.

A: steep look down from close by. The near post tapers hard from top to bottom, the dock cuts across the card diagonally and leaves the frame, and there is no horizon, so the view feels forced. B: mild view with a horizon. Rear posts shrink evenly, with beach in front, dock in the middle and sea behind, all on one plane.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera and pull back so posts stand nearly upright with little taper. Show the whole dock with a horizon line across the top third.

pairs.difference: A: slim trunk with gentle taper and a low sand line, fronds spread nearly flat to the viewer, shallow space. B: the trunk flares strongly toward the base as if seen by a wide lens from below, while fronds arch as thick swollen shells showing their undersides, and a long cast shadow pushes depth into the sand.
pairs.fix: Draw a slimmer trunk with even width from a level camera. Spread flatter fronds facing the viewer, and keep the sand low and calm, with no long shadow.

pairs.difference: A: raised close camera, the locker widens toward the top with its lid top visible, and floorboards fan out strongly from the base, so perspective is pushed. B: mild view, with near-parallel uprights, the top barely visible, and a shallow floor. Only the nearly level floorboards disagree slightly with the rising skirting line.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera to mid-locker height so the top face is hidden, keep uprights parallel, and run floorboards back gently instead of fanning out.

pairs.difference: A: stable high three-quarter view with the whole slide centred and a large tile ground reaching the pool in front, showing every top surface. B: low dramatic view, the slide sweeping large toward the viewer with the platform underside visible and tiles nearly edge-on. It is bolder but consistent, like the lively real camera shots.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera toward pool-deck level so less of the tile top shows, and turn the slide so its curve sweeps toward the viewer.

pairs.difference: A: mild tilted view, player small and flat-faced, earbuds similar in scale to it, flat background. B: forced wide-angle, the earbuds blow up at the bottom of the card, larger than the controls. The player's corners swell into a smooth rainbow on the normal lens and the cable shrinks quickly to the top.
pairs.fix: Draw the earbuds small next to the player at the same distance from the camera. Keep the player's face flat with a thin even side edge.

pairs.difference: A: the envelope and photos read as flat stacked sheets with no side thickness. planar_share 0.855 is above the real maximum of 0.679, and the normal lens is almost blank, with only thin overlap edges giving depth. B: the envelope has a rounded edge and front pocket depth, and the photos stand behind it in clear layers. Real cards, even the ticket, always show a thick edge.
pairs.fix: Give the envelope a visible thick edge along its bottom and side, and open the pocket so the photos sit deep inside it with a shadow between layers.

pairs.difference: A: the plate and wood are seen from high above with no horizon, but the watermelon stands up facing the viewer as if seen from the front, so plate and fruit do not share one view. B: lower camera, with table edge and wall line in the back, and the bowl rim and fruit agree on one angle.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera so the plate is a narrow oval, show the table's back edge against a plain wall, and sit the fruit at that same angle.

pairs.difference: A: the door is frontal but the steps and paving tip up as seen from above, and pot, lantern and bush add many foreground and side layers around a slightly bulging arch. B: a straight-on, flat door with no ground and only ivy overlapping the frame. It has one view, though planar_share 0.012 is below the real range despite clear flat panels, so that number looks like a lens failure.
pairs.fix: Keep the camera straight on and level, so the step shows only a thin top. Remove the pot and bush, leaving the door and wreath as the only layers.

pattern: Generated cards tend to use a raised, safe camera that shows more top face and a broad ground, with the whole object centred. Real cards more often have a lower or livelier view with a controlled ground line. Generated cards also add depth with extra props and scenery layers, push wide-angle swelling on near parts (earbuds, trunk base, thick target disc), and sometimes mix views, such as fruit seen from the front on a plate seen from above. Most calls here rest on modest evidence: confidence is 2 on eleven of sixteen pairs.
